analysis: Reviewed docs/developer/test.md base excerpts (lines 921-1842) and the patch hunk, which adds only documentation at head lines 2465-2485: a section on cluster service listeners after re-pairing (ClusterServicePairingChangeTests, ConsolePairingChangeChecks). The PR changes no executable code, workflow, protocol, key handling, attestation, cache storage or authorization logic, so the threat-model assets and boundaries (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-011, TB-012 and T-041, which was supplied) are not affected by it. The new text describes tests only: loopback listeners, a private home directory, no production ports or Thunderbolt interfaces, and the claim that earlier listeners refuse a re-paired peer with handshakeRejected. This is test-description prose, not a control; the real behavior lives in ClusterService sources that were not supplied. Whether those listeners truly refuse stale pairings, and whether the dial-without-lock detail has security implications, cannot be verified from this documentation-only change. The unchanged base text covers App Attest dispatch tests, native qualification, release workflow tests and prompt fixtures. I saw no new attack surface or invalidated assumptions in it, and no secrets appear. The patch excerpt is marked incomplete, but the visible hunk is documentation-only. No threat-model update is needed beyond possibly noting the cluster pairing-change behavior if the accompanying code PR alters trust boundaries. That code is outside this batch.
